correctness.rationale: All finite cactus forests factorize over edge-disjoint blocks because cycles cannot cross an articulation. Each terminal-pair connection is an intersection over local connections along a unique block route. For weighted cycles, independent Bernoulli edges conditioned on not all open reduce to positive failed-arc odds. Exhaustive terminal arrangements give strictly positive exact covariance numerators: 3-terminal ac(a+b+c+ab+bc); 4-terminal noncross ac((1+b)(1+d)(1+a+c)-1); crossing L(ac+bd)+LT-(ab+cd)(bc+ad)+Labcd, with the apparent subtraction dominated coefficientwise by LT. Identical local pairs and bridge blocks have strict positive variance. Factor products imply nonnegative covariance, strict iff a shared block. The standalone source was run and passed 4,152 exact rational/integer assertions; its finite checks are supplementary only.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper states the all-graph nonnegative covariance as Conjecture 6.2, and proves only restricted high-equal-fugacity cases (Prop. 6.1). The present all-positive-vector cactus class, with iff independence, is not implied by that result. Erickson 2012 proves edge Rayleigh negative correlation on series-parallel graphs but does not state a result for positively correlated vertex connectivity events. Targeted published published-finding corpus queries and source searches found no covering exact statement; an older equivalent block-structure result remains a real priority risk.
residual_risks: Potential older unindexed equivalent result in forest two-point correlation or graph-block probability literature, notwithstanding exact searches.

Graphical-block decomposition is classical; the new aspect claimed is the two-event weighted cycle covariance lemma and all-weight cactus strictness classification, not the block factorization itself.

value.rationale: The 2026 cited paper explicitly poses positive two-connection correlation at all weights as an open mathematical gap. Cactus graphs support arbitrarily many cycles and heterogeneous edge weights, producing a meaningful infinite class rather than a one-off calculation. The iff independence/strictness theorem identifies exact structural dependence and supplies a reusable weighted-cycle inequality. No downstream general-graph conclusion is claimed.
